message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to current air‑quality data, but you can quickly check the latest conditions in Los Angeles using a few reliable resources:

| Source | How to use it | What you’ll see |
|--------|---------------|-----------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit https://www.airnow.gov/, enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. | Current AQI value, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), and a short forecast. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to https://aqicn.org/, search for “Los Angeles”. | Real‑time AQI, historical trend graph, and health recommendations. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or your phone’s weather widget) | Look for the “Air Quality” section. | AQI, pollutant levels, and sometimes a color‑coded map. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, NBC Los Angeles) | Search “air quality Los Angeles” in their news feed. | Often include a quick summary and links to official data. |

If you’re looking for a quick snapshot right now, try AirNow or AQICN—they update every 15–30 minutes and give you both the numeric AQI and a visual indicator (green for good, yellow for moderate, orange for unhealthy for sensitive groups, red for unhealthy, etc.). If you need more detailed historical data or forecasts, those sites also provide charts and downloadable datasets.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the numbers or understanding what the AQI means for health and outdoor activities!
